decision_conditions: Due to its design and lack of sympathetic detailing, the proposed front porch would destroy a shared historic open porch feature of the properties in this section of Grove Road failing to respect the prominent principal features of the properties in the Grove Road streetscene. The proposed porch extension would detract from the host property, and the historic and architectural integrity of its contribution to the character and appearance of the Landseer Road Conservation Area. The proposal would result in significant harm to the host property and street scene in the Landseer Road Conservation Area, contrary to Policies 28 and 30 of the Sutton Local Plan 2018 and the guidance in Supplementary Planning Document 4 'Design of Residential Extensions (SPD 4).

The proposed single storey rear extension with a raised patio, by reason of its sitting on higher ground and excessive depth and eaves on the shared boundaries would appear as a disproportionate and incongruous addition that would adversely affect the character of the existing dwelling and the rear streetscene of the Landseer Road Conservation Area. The proposal is therefore contrary to Policies 28 and 30 of the Sutton Local Plan and the guidance provided in SPD4 'Design of Residential Extensions'.

The proposal, and the first floor side extension in particular, by reason of its significant reduction of the separation gap from the east boundary and undue removal of a significant part of the original heritage chimney breasts on the east elevation, would fail to preserve and enhance the original dwelling and its characteristic features that contribute to the unique design of the dwellings in this part of Landseer Road Conservation Area. Moreover, the proposed first floor side extension would unbalance the pair of semi-detached dwellings, disrupting the established visual symmetry between the two, causing significant and unacceptable harm to the character and appearance of the dwelling, the pair of semi-detached dwellings and this section of Grove Road streetscene where first floor side extensions are not a common feature. As such, the proposal is contrary to Policies 28 and 30 of the Sutton Local Plan 2018.

The proposed ground floor rear extension with a raised patio, by reason of its excessive height, eaves and depth along the shared boundaries with Nos. 134 and 138 Grove Road and proximity to the rear ground floor primary windows and the rear amenity areas of these properties, would create an un-neighbourly sense of enclosure, loss of privacy and outlook from the rear gardens and ground floor and first floor rear windows of Nos. 134 and 138, causing an adverse amenity impact to the current and future occupants of these properties. As such, the proposal is contrary to Policy 29 of Sutton Local Plan 2018.
description: Erection of front entrance porch, single storey rear extension, first floor side extension, raised patio to rear including privacy screens and roof lights to front, side and rear roofslopes.
